Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Trump administration is relaxing requirements for automakers to control pollution from gasoline-powered
cars and light trucks.
The new standards set the average for these vehicles at roughly 35 miles a gallon in the
2031 model year, down from a projected 50.4 miles per gallon under rules put in place
by the Biden administration.
President Trump claims the less stringent mileage requirements would save Americans
thousands of dollars on a new car.
American farmers have largely escaped President Trump's aggressive immigration crackdown,
but as NPR's Kirk Sigler reports, as ice sweeps continue, there's growing unease because
many still can't find enough workers.
Idaho is the nation's third largest milk and dairy producer, and the labor shortage is
even more pronounced in this sector of the farm economy because dairies operate year-round
and aren't eligible for coveted H-2A seasonal visas.
Rick Nairabout heads the dairy associations for Idaho and Washington State.
We haven't seen the worksite enforcement within agriculture, and, you know, we've been spared
there for the last year and a half or so.
But Nairabout says just as quickly his industry could fall out of favor with the Trump administration.
Dairymen had been pushing for a GOP bill that would remove the seasonal requirement for
some farmworker visas, but Congress is now in recess until after the midterms.
Kirk Sigler, NPR News, Twin Falls, Idaho.
British police say that five men arrested under counterterrorism laws near a U.S. run
or air base in England have been released on bail but are still under investigation.
Investigators haven't concluded whether the incident was state-backed.
They are investigating a possible link to Iran, Russia, or non-state-backed militant
groups.
R.A.F.
Fairford is home to long-range U.S. bombers that have been used in the Iran war and has
been the focus of anti-war protests.
Investigators say they are reopening an investigation into alleged sexual assault by members of
a fraternity at Cornell University.
Aurora Barry of Member Station WSKG reports that's after public uproar following a lawsuit
against the university, several Greek life organizations, and fraternity members.
The plaintiff in the lawsuit was a Cornell student at the time of the incident.
The lawsuit says she was drugged and sexually assaulted by seven fraternity members in 2024.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten says the plaintiff "did not allege
that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped" in her original statement.
Van Houten says the case will now go before a grand jury.
Cornell's vice president for university relations Kyle Kimball says that the university supports
the decision to reopen the investigation.
The lawsuit says Cornell didn't do enough to protect the plaintiff.
For NPR News, I'm Aurora Barry in Ithaca.
People in Mexico's Baja, California, Sur state are preparing for Hurricane Polo, which threatens
high winds, floods, and mudslides.
It's a Category 3 storm with top-sustained winds of 115 miles an hour.
It's expected to hit the Mexican mainland next.
This is NPR News.
The owners of Camp Mystic have proposed selling off the Texas Riverfront property in bankruptcy.
The plan hopes that a buyer will preserve the historic mission of the century-old private
Christian girls' camp, where 25 campers and two counselors died in a flood last year.
A buyer would likely get a portion of the camp frozen in time.
Most of the victims have fought to stop any demolition and stop repairs to preserve evidence
for their lawsuits.
The Cleveland Orchestra's strike is over after months of bargaining.
Kabir Bhatia from member station WKSU has more.
The Cleveland Orchestra and its musicians' union announced a three-year contract that
includes annual raises of 5 percent.
The increases will bring the musicians' base salary to more than $190,000.
The union requested a 25 percent raise, but management said that wasn't sustainable for
the future.
The new contract also gives members of the orchestra extra time off to help prevent repetitive
stress injuries like tendonitis and more input in the audition process.
The musicians are free to depart on a European tour.
Last week, orchestra officials said canceling the three-week tour would damage the orchestra's
finances and reputation, especially during the 25th and final season for music director
Franz Welser Most.
For NPR News, I'm Kabir Bhatia in Cleveland.
Two giant pandas have arrived in Atlanta as part of an agreement between the Chinese and
American governments.
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrived aboard a dedicated FedEx Panda Express Boeing 777.
They will be quarantined for about a month in a biosecure area of the wildlife park's
new giant panda complex.
Atlanta is one of three zoos in the U.S. to house giant pandas.
This is NPR News.
This week on NPR's Newsmakers, Tucker Carlson has broken with President Trump over the war
with Iran and says he warned the president to his face that the war would be a mistake.
And he looked at me and said, yes, you're right, but in the end, we all die anyway.
So it doesn't matter.
Tucker Carlson this week on NPR's Newsmakers.

Hurricane Polo approaches Mexico's Baja California Sur as Category 3 storm with 115 mph winds

Cleveland Orchestra ends months-long strike with three-year contract including five percent annual raises
